blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At executive level, the income statement is read as a narrative — a story about how the business is actually performing and, more importantly, what is shaping its direction. The numbers are the words; the story is what matters. A 5% revenue growth with shrinking gross margin is a very different story from a 5% growth with stable margin, even though the headline looks identical.

What the senior finance leader brings to the room is the ability to tell that story honestly — neither more optimistic than the numbers allow, nor more pessimistic than the situation deserves. It is the calibration that matters: the ability to present the narrative in a way that sharpens the team's judgement rather than flatters or frightens it.

It is the story, not the numbers, that the board remembers a week later. A well-told P&L story shapes every strategic conversation for the following month. A poorly told one quietly fades, taking any chance of real decision-making with it.

items.q: According to the text, why can two companies with identical 5% revenue growth tell very different stories?
options: Because the headline figure is always misleading
Because the gross margin may be stable in one and shrinking in the other
Because one has a larger board than the other
Because revenue growth is never comparable between firms
items.why: "A 5% revenue growth with shrinking gross margin is a very different story from a 5% growth with stable margin."

items.q: What does the author identify as the senior finance leader's key skill?
options: Presenting only the headline figures
The ability to simplify the numbers
Optimism about future performance
Calibration — telling the story honestly, neither over- nor under-stated
items.why: "It is the calibration that matters… neither more optimistic than the numbers allow, nor more pessimistic than the situation deserves."

items.q: The cleft construction "It is the story, not the numbers, that the board remembers" is used to emphasise that…
options: the numbers are unimportant and should be ignored
what endures with the board is the narrative, not the raw figures
the board has a poor memory for detail
stories are always more accurate than numbers
items.why: Inferência: o cleft realça a narrativa como o que permanece — sem afirmar que os números não importam.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: A misjudged story can undermine real decision-making
A P&L presentation is complete once the figures are accurate
The margin trend can matter more than the headline
How a P&L is framed affects the decisions that follow
items.why: Inferência: o texto inteiro argumenta que os números sozinhos não bastam — a narrativa e a calibração são o que conta.

items.q: What does the phrase "taking any chance of real decision-making with it" suggest about a poorly told P&L story?
options: Its failure also costs the organisation the opportunity to decide well
It forces the board to recalculate the numbers
It merely delays the next meeting
It has no consequence beyond the presentation itself
items.why: Inferência: quando a história se apaga, a chance de decidir de verdade se apaga junto — o custo vai além da apresentação.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie contando a história do P&L numa revisão executiva mensal. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So the headline this month is a clean five per cent revenue growth, and I can see the relief around the table. But I'd ask you to hold that reaction for a moment, because the story underneath is a little less comfortable.

What has actually happened is that we grew the top line by discounting — and gross margin slipped almost two points while we did it. So it isn't the demand that's driving the number; it's the price we're willing to accept. Strip out the promotional accounts and the underlying growth is closer to one per cent.

Now, I'm not here to frighten anyone. This is entirely fixable, and a two-point compression is not a crisis. What it is, is a signal — and my job is to put it in front of you honestly rather than let a good headline flatter us into doing nothing.

So my recommendation is that we treat next quarter as a margin quarter, not a volume one. If we chase the same headline again by cutting price, we'll book the growth and quietly lose the business underneath it.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is Sophie's main point about this month's 5% revenue growth?
options: It was driven by genuine new demand
It should be celebrated without qualification
It was achieved through discounting, while gross margin slipped
It exceeded the board's target comfortably
items.why: "we grew the top line by discounting — and gross margin slipped almost two points."

items.q: What is the underlying growth once the promotional accounts are stripped out?
options: The same five per cent
Around two per cent
Slightly negative
Around one per cent
items.why: "Strip out the promotional accounts and the underlying growth is closer to one per cent."

items.q: When Sophie says she is "not here to frighten anyone," she is signalling that…
options: the board should ignore the margin figure
she wants the concern taken seriously but proportionately
the numbers are too complex to explain
the situation is a full-blown crisis
items.why: Inferência: ela calibra a mensagem — é um sinal a tratar, não um pânico; nem lisonjeia nem assusta.

items.q: What does Sophie mean by "we'll book the growth and quietly lose the business underneath it"?
options: The board will reject the figures
The revenue will be recorded incorrectly
The reported growth will mask an erosion of the real, profitable business
The business will grow faster than expected
items.why: Inferência: repetir o desconto entrega o número na manchete, mas corrói silenciosamente a margem e a saúde do negócio.

items.q: How would you best describe Sophie's approach in this update?
options: Reassuring to the point of dismissing the issue
Purely technical, with no recommendation
Honest and calibrated — flagging a signal without exaggerating it
Alarmist and pessimistic
items.why: Inferência: ela apresenta o problema com honestidade e propõe um caminho — a calibração central da lição.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The board remembers the narrative, not the spreadsheet." A narrative here is…
options: a footnote in the annual report
the coherent story the figures are made to tell
an unstructured list of numbers
a fictional account with no basis in fact
items.why: Narrative = narrativa: a história coerente que os números contam.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The ___ figure looked strong, but the margin trend beneath it told another story."
options: calibration
headline
judgement
narrative
items.why: Headline = manchete: o número de destaque, que aqui esconde a tendência da margem.

items.q: "It is the calibration that matters." In this context, calibration means…
options: rounding the figures to the nearest thousand
adjusting the accounting software
pitching the message so it is neither overstated nor understated
aligning the report with regulation
items.why: Calibration = calibração: ajustar o tom para não exagerar nem minimizar.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A clear P&L story should ___ the team's judgement, not blunt it."
options: sharpen
frighten
flatter
fade
items.why: To sharpen = afiar; o oposto de 'blunt' (embotar) no contexto.

items.q: "A poorly told P&L story quietly fades." To fade here means to…
options: become brighter over time
be formally withdrawn
gradually lose impact and be forgotten
be openly rejected by the board
items.why: To fade = desaparecer, perder força pouco a pouco na memória do grupo.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões financeiras e revisões de resultados. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The CFO still has to sign off on the revised forecast." To sign off on means to…
options: circulate it for comment
reject it outright
present it to the market
formally approve it
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Two directors pushed back on the margin narrative." They…
options: resisted or challenged it
endorsed it immediately
asked to see it later
rewrote the whole report
items.why: Push back on = resistir, questionar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Trimming a point of price won't move the needle on profitability." This means it will…
options: reverse the trend overnight
not make a noticeable difference
be impossible to measure
trigger resistance from the team
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.

items.q: "The team agreed to defend margin but never followed through." They…
options: handed it to finance
documented it thoroughly
carried it to completion
failed to see it through to the end
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado; aqui, o que NÃO fizeram.

items.q: "Let's not let a good headline gloss over the margin compression." To gloss over means to…
options: escalate to the board
highlight aggressively
explain in full detail
treat a problem as unimportant or hide it
items.why: Gloss over = passar por cima, minimizar ou disfarçar um problema.
